introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2025. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) OR SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Non-programmable electronic calculators and Mathematical Formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) The events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A)=\dfrac{3}{10}$, $P(B)=\dfrac25$ and $P(A\cup B)=\dfrac35$. Find $P(A\cap B)$. *[2 marks]*
themes: probability of unions and intersections of events
tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(c) With $P(A)=\dfrac{3}{10}$, $P(B)=\dfrac25$ and $P(A\cup B)=\dfrac35$, find $P(A'\cap B)$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The event $B$ is split into the part inside $A$ and the part outside $A$:

$P(B)=P(A\cap B)+P(A'\cap B)\Rightarrow P(A'\cap B)=\dfrac25-\dfrac1{10}=\dfrac4{10}-\dfrac1{10}=\dfrac3{10}.$

**$P(A'\cap B)=\dfrac3{10}$.**
themes: probability of unions and intersections of events

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) In a certain school of 200 students, 80 are boys and 120 are girls. 30% of the boys and 60% of the girls play handball. A student $X$ is selected at random from the school. Find the probability that:

(a) $X$ is a boy who plays handball. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Boys who play handball: $30\%\times80=24$.

$P(\text{boy who plays handball})=\dfrac{24}{200}=\dfrac3{25}=0.12.$

**$\dfrac3{25}$ (or $0.12$).**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) In the same school (200 students: 80 boys, 120 girls; 30% of the boys and 60% of the girls play handball), find the probability that $X$ plays handball. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Girls who play handball: $60\%\times120=72$. Total who play handball: $24+72=96$.

$P(X\text{ plays handball})=\dfrac{96}{200}=\dfrac{12}{25}=0.48.$

**$\dfrac{12}{25}$ (or $0.48$).**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) In the same school, find the probability that $X$ is a boy or plays handball. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $B$ be 'is a boy' and $H$ be 'plays handball': $P(B)=\dfrac{80}{200}$, $P(H)=\dfrac{96}{200}$, $P(B\cap H)=\dfrac{24}{200}$.

$P(B\cup H)=P(B)+P(H)-P(B\cap H)=\dfrac{80+96-24}{200}=\dfrac{152}{200}=\dfrac{19}{25}=0.76.$

Check by counting: 80 boys plus the 72 girls who play handball give $152$ students.

**$\dfrac{19}{25}$ (or $0.76$).**
